newsitem.title: USA: CME hog and pork belly futures end mixed.
newsitem.headline: CME hog and pork belly futures end mixed.

text.p: CME live hog and pork belly futures closed mixed as most traders spent the latter half of Tuesday's abbreviated session balancing accounts, floor sources said.

February hogs closed slightly higher. Some traders said Friday's USDA Hogs and Pigs Report may be slightly bullish for hog futures. Analysts surveyed by Reuters expect the report to show fewer hogs as of December 1 than a year ago, but it should also show production is expanding.
Analysts' estimates for all hogs as of December 1 averaged 98.4 percent of a year ago, kept for breeding estimates averaged 101.6 and kept for marketing estimates averaged 97.5.
Pork belly futures closed mostly steady to higher on light pre-holiday short covering. However, several traders cautioned the market could drop sharply if Friday's report contains any bearish data.
"God forbid if we get anything bearish," said one trader. "78 is a high level. You have to have good news."
February pork bellies have traded near 78.00 cents per lb since mid-November, rising from an October low in the mid-60s.
Hog futures closed up 0.175 cent to off 0.400 cent with February up 0.175 at 76.100 cents a lb. Pork bellies closed down 0.125 to up 0.200 cent with February up 0.150 at 78.325.
CME livestock markets will be closed Wednesday for Christmas and will reopen Thursday.
